issues.legal_issue: A substantive determination made in an earlier suit can operate as res judicata in a later suit even when the earlier court also found that the plaintiff was not entitled to sue, if the substantive issue was directly tried and no preliminary issue made its determination unnecessary.
material_facts: In the earlier suit, the plaintiff claimed that an estate-holder had only a life interest under a will and a related letter, and sought relief concerning the estate.

The earlier court considered the nature of the estate in detail, held that the estate-holder had obtained absolute ownership, and found that the plaintiff had no present interest entitling him to sue.
The earlier court did not dispose of the case on a preliminary issue that made examination of the estate-holder’s rights unnecessary.
In the later suit, the plaintiff again based his claim on the will and letter, and the court held that the earlier determination barred the claim.
issues.conclusion: The earlier decision operated as res judicata on the nature of the estate, and the later suit was barred.
issues.legal_principle: Where a court’s final decision rests on determinations of more than one point, each independently sufficient to support that decision, each determination operates as res judicata between the parties. The Court applied Vithal Yeshwant Jathar v. Shikandarkhan Mukhtum-khan, [1963] 2 S.C.R. 285 at 290, and explained and distinguished Shankarlal v. Hiralal, A.I.R. 1950 P.C. 80. It also explained that if a plaint on its face discloses a bar such as failure to comply with section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court should reject it without trying the merits; where the plaint does not facially disclose that bar, the court may decide the issues raised, and its substantive determinations may bind the parties in later litigation.

rule.if: subsequent_suit and same_parties_or_privies and same_substantive_issue_relitigated and prior_court_decided_substantive_issue and not preliminary_issue_made_substantive_decision_unnecessary

predicates.subsequent_suit: The proceeding is a later suit in which a claim is again advanced.
predicates.same_parties_or_privies: The parties to the later suit are the same as, or legally represented by, parties to the earlier suit.
predicates.same_substantive_issue_relitigated: The later suit raises for determination the same substantive issue that was raised in the earlier suit.
predicates.prior_court_decided_substantive_issue: The earlier court tried and determined the substantive issue between the parties.
predicates.preliminary_issue_made_substantive_decis: A preliminary issue disposed of the earlier suit in a way that made deciding the substantive issue unnecessary.
predicates.subsequent_claim_is_barred: The later claim cannot be tried because the earlier determination binds the parties.

issues.definition: When a later suit between the same parties or their privies raises an issue already decided substantively in an earlier suit, and no preliminary issue made that decision unnecessary, the later claim is barred.
